intro_cards.texto: The Egyptians believed that, when you died, the gods weighed your heart on a scale.
On the other side they placed a feather: the feather of Maat, goddess of truth and justice.
If your heart weighed LESS than the feather, you had lived well: you went to Aaru, a paradise of endless fields.
If it weighed MORE, it was devoured by Ammit, a monster part crocodile, part lion and part hippopotamus. And you vanished forever.
You are Nakht, a farmer who lived by the river Nile. You have just died.

intro_mision: Survive 3 nights against the creatures of Ammit.
Do good deeds: your heart gets lighter.
In the end, your heart must weigh less than the feather (under 50).

intro: Anubis: I am Anubis, guardian of the dead. I weigh the hearts.
Anubis: Nakht... your heart weighed exactly the same as the feather. That has never happened before.
Anubis: Neither good nor bad. I cannot judge you like this.
Anubis: I return you to life for three days. What you do will decide which way your heart tips.
Anubis: But Ammit does not want to go hungry. Every night she will send her creatures after you.
Anubis: Thoth, scribe of the gods. You recorded this judgment. You will go with him and write down everything he does.
Thoth: ...As you command. I am Thoth, Nakht. Wherever you go, I go. Everything you do will be on my papyrus, and in the end Anubis will read it.

pesaje_intro: Anubis: Three days have passed. Let us see what your heart weighs now.
liviano: Anubis: Lighter than the feather. The road to Aaru opens... a little.
Thoth: I'll write that in my best handwriting.
empate: Anubis: In balance once again. Your deeds still decide nothing.
Thoth: What a stubborn heart you have.
pesado: Anubis: Your heart weighs more than the feather. Ammit can already smell your name.
Thoth: There is still time. Not much.
ba: A memory of your ba returns, like a bird with a human face.
A river. A child laughing on the bank, holding a papyrus stalk.
The child turns around. He has Iry's eyes.
Thoth: ...So you are starting to remember.

ya_robado: Thoth: The offering is gone. I hope you remember that at the weighing.
bloqueado: Thoth: Offerings for Maat. Don't even think about it.
robar: Thoth: That offering isn't yours, farmer.
Nakht takes the offering from the altar without anyone seeing.
Thoth: I saw it. I always see.
dejar: Thoth: Good. Maat also watches what you don't do.

intro: Meret (sorpresa): You... are walking? The dead should not walk.
Meret: I am Meret, priestess of this temple. Here we serve Maat, goddess of truth and justice.
Meret (feliz): Maat judges what you do, not whether you breathe. Perhaps there is still some good in you.
Meret: I need flax to weave bandages. Bring me three bundles and you will earn my trust.
Thoth: Flax is sown with seed 2. It takes two days to grow: plant it today.
recordatorio: Meret: Three bundles of flax. Bandages don't weave themselves.
mision_completa: Meret: Real flax. With this we weave the bandages for those who depart.
Meret (feliz): I'm starting to think you're not a threat, farmer. Starting, I said.
repeat: Meret: May Maat find you in balance.
escarabajo: Meret (triste): Wait. Tonight the air smells of something worse than shadows.
Meret: Take this heart scarab. It was placed on the chest of the dead so the heart would not speak against them.
Meret: For you it will work differently: if you fall tonight, it will raise you once.
Thoth: Equip it with Q. And try not to need it.
defendiste: Meret: Last night I saw you fight in front of our homes. You lost part of your harvest for us.
Meret (feliz): Maat saw it too. That carries weight.
abandonaste: Meret (enojo): Last night the shadows got into the village. Where were you?
Meret (enojo): Ah, looking after your wheat. Of course.

charla: Meret: Every morning I sweep the temple courtyard, even if no one comes. Maat doesn't need an audience.
Meret: Did you know the feather of Maat is an ostrich feather? White, light, straight. That's how a heart should be.
Meret: As a girl I counted the stars from the temple roof. I always got forty-two. Like the judges of the Duat.
Meret: Farmers think priests don't eat. We do. Bread, onions and a lot of patience.
Meret: Last night I dreamed of the Nile in flood. A good sign. Or so I want to believe.
ya_charlaste: Meret: We've already talked today, Nakht. Go to your fields; tomorrow you'll have more to tell me.
regalo_ama: Meret (feliz): Flax! This is what the sacred bandages are woven from. I'll keep it in the sanctuary. Thank you, truly.
regalo_gusta: Meret (feliz): Papyrus... it will do for copying prayers. You're thoughtful.
regalo_normal: Meret: Thank you. I'll share it with whoever needs it.
ya_regalaste: Meret: You already gave me something today. Keep the rest; your farm needs it more than I do.
nada_que_regalar: Meret: You're not carrying any harvest. It doesn't matter: your company is an offering too.
nivel1: Meret: There used to be seven priests. When the temple cracked, the others fled downriver.
Meret: I stayed. Someone had to light the lamp every night.
Meret: Here, flax seeds. If you ever want to help me rebuild this place, the sanctuary bandages will come first.
nivel2: Meret: Nakht... there's something I haven't told you.
Meret (triste): I was the one who prepared your body for burial. I washed you with natron, I started wrapping you in linen...
Meret (triste): But that night the shadows came. I ran and left you half-wrapped, with the rites unfinished.
Meret (triste): Maybe that's why your heart was left undecided on the scale. Because of me.
Meret: This amulet of Maat was meant for your chest. Wear it now. It will give you strength.
nivel3: Meret (triste): For years I doubted Maat. I thought she had abandoned us, that the scale was a children's tale.
Meret (sorpresa): And then a dead man came back to plow the earth, to defend strangers, to rebuild a temple that wasn't even his.
Meret (feliz): You gave me back my faith. This feather is from my first day as a priestess. Now it's yours.
templo_intro: Meret: The temple is falling apart. With harvests and deben we could restore it, piece by piece.
Meret: And believe me: Maat rewards those who raise her house.
templo_hecho_columnas: Meret (feliz): The columns stand again! I can feel the temple breathing once more.
Meret: Maat blesses you: your body will take more blows.
templo_hecho_estatua: Meret: The statue of Maat watches over us again. Her justice guides your defenses: they'll hit harder.
templo_hecho_estandartes: Meret: The banners fly above the pylon. Even the river seems happier.
Meret: Your fields will receive Maat's flood more often.
templo_hecho_santuario: Meret (sorpresa): The sanctuary shines. I haven't seen this light in years.
Meret (feliz): Nakht... the temple is complete. Maat looks kindly on you. Your heart is lighter.
templo_falta: Meret: You don't have what's needed yet. Check the list: harvests and deben.
templo_completo: Meret: The temple is complete thanks to you. Come pray whenever you like; I'm not alone anymore.

intro: Ptahmose (feliz): A new face on my dock! I'm Ptahmose, river merchant.
Ptahmose: I buy your harvests and sell you seeds. And if you stay a while, I'll tell you stories from other cities.
Thoth: Here you pay in 'deben': the copper money of Egypt.
repeat: Ptahmose: Bringing anything to sell today?
vender_vacio: Ptahmose: Come back when your bag is full of something other than sand.
vender_exito: Ptahmose (feliz): Good deal. The river always gives to those who know how to wait.
sin_dinero: Ptahmose (enojo): With that purse you couldn't buy the air on this dock.
compra_ok: Ptahmose (feliz): Seeds from the finest silt in Kemet. Well, the second finest.
rumores: Ptahmose: They say in Thebes a scribe fell asleep on his papyrus and woke up with the text written backwards.
Thoth: That happened to me. Once. Centuries ago.
Ptahmose: In the delta they say Apep, the serpent of chaos, attacks Ra's boat every night.
Thoth: That one is true. And every morning the sun rises again, so Apep loses. Always.
Ptahmose: The nobles are buried with shabtis, little figures that will work the land for them in the afterlife.
Thoth: You have no shabtis, farmer. You'll have to harvest Aaru with your own hands.

charla: Ptahmose: The price of wheat in Thebes doubled! Or so my cousin says. My cousin lies a lot.
Ptahmose: I once sold a donkey to a priest of Ptah. The donkey was wiser than he was.
Ptahmose: See this ring? Gold-plated copper. But don't tell anyone.
Ptahmose: Trade is trust, my friend. That's why I always count what I'm paid twice.
Ptahmose: At night I lock up with three bolts. Two for thieves and one for Ammit.
ya_charlaste: Ptahmose: You've had enough free chatter out of me for today! Come back tomorrow.
regalo_ama: Ptahmose (sorpresa): First-rate papyrus! In Memphis they'd pay me in silver for this. Are you sure you're giving it to me? No regrets!
regalo_gusta: Ptahmose (feliz): Wheat. Honest and golden, like me. Well, almost like me.
regalo_normal: Ptahmose: A gift... what a strange custom among merchants! Thank you.
ya_regalaste: Ptahmose: One a day, friend. Otherwise I'll start thinking you want something.
nada_que_regalar: Ptahmose (enojo): Give me what? Air? Bring me harvests.
nivel1: Ptahmose (feliz): I like you, Nakht. The living haggle; at least you work.
Ptahmose: From today on, friend's price on seeds. Don't tell Iry, he'll bleed me dry.
nivel2: Ptahmose (triste): I'm going to tell you something I've never told anyone. Not even my wife.
Ptahmose (triste): When I was young... I was a tomb robber. I'd sneak into the mastabas at night and take amulets, rings, anything that shone.
Ptahmose (triste): When I saw Ammit's creatures on the first night, I knew they were coming for people like me.
Ptahmose (feliz): Take these coins. I earned them honestly. Almost all of them.
nivel3: Ptahmose (triste): Last night I went back to the necropolis. Alone.
Ptahmose (triste): I returned the last amulet I stole, a scarab-shaped one, to the tomb I took it from.
Ptahmose (sorpresa): I could swear I heard someone sigh with relief. Maybe it was me.
Ptahmose (feliz): From today on I'll buy your harvests at a better price. An honest merchant, who'd have thought?

intro: Iry (sorpresa): Hey! Is it true you were dead? That's so cool! I'm Iry.
Iry: Thoth, who is Anubis? Why does he have a dog's head?
Thoth: A jackal's, Iry. Anubis is the god who looks after the dead and the cemeteries. That's why he saw Nakht first.
Iry (sorpresa): And does he bark?
Thoth (sarcasmo): ...Not that I know of.
repeat: Iry: When I grow up I want to tend crops like you. Or be a scribe. I haven't decided.
dia2: Iry (sorpresa): Last night I saw shadows from the roof! Thoth, what are they?
Thoth: The sheut. To the Egyptians, the shadow was also part of a person. These are shadows with no owner.
Iry (triste): That's scary... but so interesting.
dia3: Iry (triste): Nakht... did we know each other before? I feel like I've seen you by the river.
Iry (sorpresa): Thoth? Why aren't you saying anything? You always say something.
senet_pedido: Iry (triste): Nakht... I lost my senet piece playing in the necropolis. My dad carved it for me!
Thoth: Senet is a very old board game. The Egyptians said it was like the soul's journey after death.
Iry: Will you bring it back? I'm scared to go there alone.
Thoth: The necropolis is the cemetery, to the south. Look for something shiny.
senet_gracias: Iry (feliz): My piece! Thank you, thank you!
Iry (feliz): When I grow up I'm going to beat you at senet. You'll see.

charla: Iry: Today I learned to write my name in hieroglyphs. It's a duck, a mouth and an arm. I think.
Iry: Have you ever seen a hippo up close? I have. Well, from far away. Well, in a painting.
Iry: My mom says not to talk to dead people. But you're a nice dead person.
Iry: If I were pharaoh I'd ban onions. And naps.
Iry: The temple cat looks at me funny. I think it's a spy for Bastet.
ya_charlaste: Iry: We already played today! Tomorrow I'll tell you another secret. A real one.
regalo_ama: Iry (feliz): Wheat?! My mom is going to make honey bread! You're the best dead person in the world!
regalo_gusta: Iry (feliz): Ooh, thanks. I'm going to make a little boat out of this.
regalo_normal: Iry: For me? I'll hide it in my secret treasure.
ya_regalaste: Iry (feliz): You already gave me a present today! My mom says not to be greedy.
nada_que_regalar: Iry: Were you going to give me something? You don't have anything... It doesn't matter!
nivel1: Iry (feliz): I'll tell you a secret: I want to be your apprentice. Here, wheat seeds. I saved them for you.
nivel2: Iry (triste): Nakht... one night my dad went to the necropolis to look for a lost dog. He never came back.
Iry (triste): Everyone says Ammit took him. I don't believe it.
Iry (feliz): Starting tomorrow I'll water your crops at dawn, before you wake up. That way you have more time to fight.
nivel3: Iry (sorpresa): Last night I saw him. A bird with a man's face, sitting on the roof. It had my dad's smile.
Iry (feliz): That was his ba, right? He told me he was okay. That the scale had found him just.
Iry (sorpresa): And he told me something for you: "The Herald fears the one who walks with a light heart".
Iry (feliz): Don't cry, Nakht. Nice dead people don't cry.

thot.inicio: I'm Thoth, your scribe. Move with WASD. Your OBJECTIVES are at the top right.
thot.arar: Face a square of dark earth and press E to till it.
thot.sembrar: E again to sow. 1, 2 and 3 choose the seed.
thot.regar: E once more to water it.
thot.regado: Good. It will grow through the day and the night.
thot.aldeanos: The village is to the upper right. Those with a ! want to talk to you.
thot.atardecer: The sun is setting. Your tools become weapons: get ready.
thot.noche1: (sorpresa) Here they come! Click to attack, Space to dodge.
thot.cultivo_perdido: Ammit's spawn are going for your crops! Protect them.
thot.vida_baja: Your life is fading. Dodge, back off, or equip the Ankh with Q.
thot.amanecer: You survived. Let me read you what I wrote down tonight.
thot.dia2: Harvest, sell to Ptahmose and use the deben on defenses.
thot.defensa: See those stone pedestals by the field? Press E on one to build a defense.
thot.altar_d2: Nobody is guarding the temple altar today. It holds valuable offerings... Taking them would make you rich. And your heart, heavier.
thot.noche2: (sorpresa) Nakht! Some shadows are heading for the village and others for your crops. You can't be in both places. What will you protect?
thot.aldea_salvada: The village holds. Your crops... well. Wheat grows back; people don't.
thot.dia3: Last day. Something big is coming tonight. Meret is waiting for you at the temple.
thot.noche3: This is the great night. The Herald of Ammit is coming, her strongest messenger. Hold on.
thot.jefe: (sorpresa) The Herald! Crocodile head, lion body, hippo hindquarters. Just like its mistress. Watch out for its charge.
thot.jefe_mitad: It's wounded and furious! Keep going.
thot.jefe_muerto: It fell. Ammit will have to wait... for now.
thot.derrota: You were nearly devoured. Anubis raised you again, but it won't be free.
thot.estatua: A statue of Anubis. He protects the necropolis; today he protects your wheat.
thot.brasero: (sarcasmo) Sacred fire. Shadows don't like light. Nobody likes getting burned, really.
thot.escarabajo_uso: The scarab gave you back your breath. Don't count on it twice tonight.
thot.muro: (sarcasmo) Mudbrick: mud, straw and sun. All of Egypt was built this way, except what was made of stone to impress people.
thot.cultivo_atacado: (sorpresa) A spawn is eating your harvest! Look at the red bar over the plot: hit it before it empties.
thot.corazon_explica: See the scale at the top? That's your heart. Under 50 = light, good. Over 50 = heavy, bad. Your deeds move it.
thot.shabti: A shabti! The Egyptians buried these little figures so they would work for them in the afterlife. {n} of 5 so far.
thot.shabtis_todos: (sorpresa) All five shabtis! Ptahmose would pay well... fate already paid you. And Maat notices.
thot.senet_encontrado: Iry's senet piece. Take it to him: he's in the village.
thot.campamento_noche: (sarcasmo) Nights aren't for resting, Nakht. Nights are for fighting.
thot.ofrenda: An offering to Maat. Your heart weighs a little less.
thot.misterio_d2: Your judgment... There's something on my papyrus from that day that doesn't add up. I'll tell you later. Maybe.
thot.misterio_d3: Nakht. If your heart tied, it wasn't by chance. But it's not my place to tell you. Not yet.
thot.estado_pluma: Look at your scale: you're lighter than the feather. Maat smiles on you. Make the most of it.
thot.estado_equilibrio: (sarcasmo) Back in balance. Neither saint nor monster. Which, believe me, is the most common thing in my records.
thot.estado_sombra: (sarcasmo) Your heart is darkening. Yes, you hit harder. No, that's not a compliment.
thot.estado_hambre: Nakht... Ammit is already licking her teeth. That power you feel is HER hunger. Think about the weighing.
thot.iry_riega: (sarcasmo) Iry came by at dawn and watered {n} of your crops. That boy likes you more than his onions.
thot.templo_objetivo: Meret can restore the temple if you bring her harvests and deben. Each part brings a blessing.
thot.amistad_explica: Chat with the villagers every day and give them gifts. Friends share secrets... and help.
thot.estacion_peret: Peret: the land rises out of the water, black and soft. The Egyptians called their country Kemet, 'the black land', because of this.
thot.estacion_shemu: (sarcasmo) Shemu: heat, harvest and full pockets. And the desert, which is hungry too.
thot.estacion_akhet: Akhet: the Nile overflows. Nobody works the riverbank these days; the river waters everything for you. Watch what crawls out of the water.
thot.akhet_riego: The high water reached your fields: no need to water today.
thot.libre_inicio: (sarcasmo) Shall we go on? The Herald will return every time a season ends, stronger. And I keep writing everything down, of course.
thot.amb_necropolis: The necropolis. Here sleep those who already faced the scale. Walk with respect... and quickly.
thot.amb_rio: (sarcasmo) The Nile. It gives life, food and, now and then, a crocodile. Sobek says hello.
thot.amb_templo: The temple of Maat. It keeps the idea that the world has an order. Lately, with cracks.
amb_quieto: (sarcasmo) Meditating? Fields don't get watered with thoughts.
(sarcasmo) If you stand still much longer, someone will mistake you for a statue. And leave you offerings.
(sarcasmo) Noting: 'Nakht contemplates the horizon'. Very poetic. Not very productive.
thot.amb_esquiva: (sarcasmo) Practicing for the Opet festival? Because there's nothing to dodge in daylight.
thot.amb_combo: (sorpresa) Ten hits in a row! I'm writing that one in big letters.
thot.amb_rico: (sarcasmo) Ptahmose is smiling. That's almost never good news for your purse. Today, miraculously, it is.
thot.amb_50: Fifty creatures sent back to the Duat. Ammit must be drafting a formal complaint.
thot.amb_noche_larga: (sarcasmo) The night is long, but you're stubborn. Good combination.
recuerdos: Thoth remembers: they say I invented writing. When I showed it to the king, he feared people would stop remembering because they trusted my letters. He had a point.
(sarcasmo) Thoth remembers: I once beat the Moon at senet. I won five days of her light, and that's how the year got 365. You're welcome.
Thoth remembers: when Set tore Osiris apart, I helped Isis find the words to bring him back to life. Words heal too.
Thoth remembers: I am the scribe of the judgment. When a heart is weighed, I write down the result. I have never been wrong. Except, perhaps, once.
Thoth remembers: the ibis walks through the mud searching for what is hidden. That's why I wear its head. I look for what others don't see.
(triste) Thoth remembers: your weighing, Nakht. I wrote 'tie' with a trembling hand. My hand never trembles.
Thoth remembers: Anubis didn't send me only to watch you. He sent me to understand why the scale hesitated. I think I know now: your story wasn't finished being written.
(sarcasmo) Thoth remembers: you ask why I'm still here if the order has been carried out. Let's say I like the way you write. With spelling mistakes, but I like it.
